text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 0.33% today to $388.38, extending a decline that's seen the stock fall 2.77% over two weeks. The broader pressure comes from conflicting signals in the oil market: while crude prices rose modestly on Thursday as traders assessed potential U.S.-Iran diplomatic progress, refinery margins have compressed over the past week as U.S. oil prices ($96.41/barrel) have lagged sharply behind global oil prices ($114.89/barrel). Refiners like Marathon profit on the difference between what they pay for crude and what they sell refined products for—that gap has narrowed, which directly pressures their earnings outlook.

The two-week slide also reflects industry headwinds beyond day-to-day oil price swings. Talk of a potential diesel export ban and ongoing Middle East tensions have created uncertainty around refining demand and margins, while refineries are already running at 94% capacity with substantial crude and product inventories on hand—signs that demand may not be growing as fast as supply availability.
